headline: ThinkWorld reports human-video transfer with imagined action dynamics
summary: ThinkWorld represents action reasoning as discrete motion tokens shared across human and robot data, predicts the future state induced by those tokens, and uses agreement with observed futures as a training-time reinforcement signal. In arXiv v1, the authors report 60/60 in-domain and 52/60 out-of-distribution successes over three bimanual robot tasks. Table 6 reports 94.4% unweighted macro success across six settings and 93.3% pooled micro success (112/120 trials); MolmoAct2 is the strongest reported robot baseline at 62.2% macro and 60.0% micro. The paper also reports 55.6% average success on LIBERO-PRO versus 48.5% for VLA-JEPA. These paper-reported results are not independently reproduced; robot evaluation includes task-specific adaptation and fine-tuning, and training uses one seed.
